title_en: Asset Appraisal Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of regulating asset appraisal activities, protecting the lawful rights and interests of parties to asset appraisal and the public interest, promoting the healthy development of the asset appraisal industry, and maintaining the order of the socialist market economy.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "asset appraisal" (hereinafter referred to as "appraisal") means a professional service activity in which an appraisal institution and its appraisal professionals, upon engagement, evaluate and estimate the value of immovable property, movable property, intangible assets, enterprise value, asset losses or other economic rights and interests, and issue an appraisal report.

Article 3 Where a natural person, legal person or any other organization needs to determine the value of the appraisal subject, it may voluntarily engage an appraisal institution to conduct an appraisal.
Where, for matters involving state-owned assets or the public interest, laws or administrative regulations provide that an appraisal is required (hereinafter referred to as "statutory appraisal"), the appraisal institution shall be engaged according to law.

Article 4 An appraisal institution and its appraisal professionals shall comply with laws, administrative regulations and appraisal standards in conducting business, and shall adhere to the principles of independence, objectivity and impartiality.
An appraisal institution and its appraisal professionals conducting business according to law shall be protected by law.
Article 5 An appraisal professional engaging in appraisal business shall join an appraisal institution and may only conduct business in one appraisal institution.

Article 6 The appraisal industry may, according to law, establish trade associations by professional field, implement self-discipline management, and shall be subject to the supervision of the relevant appraisal administrative departments and public oversight.

Article 7 The relevant appraisal administrative departments under the State Council shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, supervise and administer the appraisal industry.
The relevant appraisal administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the city with districts level shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, supervise and administer the appraisal industry within their respective administrative regions.

Article 8 Appraisal professionals include appraisers and other appraisal practitioners who possess professional knowledge and practical experience in appraisal.
An appraiser refers to an appraisal professional who has passed the appraiser qualification examination. The State shall determine the professional categories of appraisers based on the needs of economic and social development.

Article 9 The relevant national appraisal trade associations shall, in accordance with State regulations, organize and implement the national unified examination for appraiser qualification.
Citizens with a college degree or higher from an institution of higher education may take the national unified examination for appraiser qualification.
Article 10 The relevant national appraisal trade associations shall publish the list of appraisers on their websites and update it in real time.

Article 11 No person who has been subjected to criminal punishment for an intentional crime, or for a negligent crime committed in the course of engaging in appraisal, finance, accounting or auditing activities, and for whom less than five years have elapsed since the date of completion of the execution of the punishment, may engage in appraisal business.

Article 15 An appraisal institution shall, according to law, adopt a partnership or company form and employ appraisal professionals to conduct appraisal business.
An appraisal institution in the form of a partnership shall have at least two appraisers; at least two-thirds of its partners shall be appraisers who have at least three years of practice experience and have not been subjected to a penalty of suspension from practice within the most recent three years.
An appraisal institution in the form of a company shall have at least eight appraisers and at least two shareholders, of whom at least two-thirds shall be appraisers who have at least three years of practice experience and have not been subjected to a penalty of suspension from practice within the most recent three years.
Where an appraisal institution has only two partners or shareholders, both partners or shareholders shall be appraisers who have at least three years of practice experience and have not been subjected to a penalty of suspension from practice within the most recent three years.

Article 16 To establish an appraisal institution, an application for registration shall be made to the administrative department for industry and commerce. The appraisal institution shall, within thirty days from the date of obtaining the business license, file a record with the relevant appraisal administrative department. The appraisal administrative department shall promptly announce the recordation of the appraisal institution to the public.

Article 17 An appraisal institution shall conduct business independently, objectively and impartially according to law, establish and improve a quality control system, and ensure that appraisal reports are objective, truthful and reasonable.
An appraisal institution shall establish and improve internal management systems, supervise whether its appraisal professionals comply with laws, administrative regulations and appraisal standards, and shall be responsible for their professional conduct.
An appraisal institution shall accept supervision and inspection according to law and truthfully provide appraisal archives and relevant information.

Article 18 Where a client refuses to provide or fails to truthfully provide the ownership certificates, financial accounting information and other materials required for carrying out the appraisal business, the appraisal institution shall have the right to refuse the client's request to perform the contract according to law.

Article 19 Where a client requests the issuance of a false appraisal report or there are other circumstances of illegal interference with the appraisal result, the appraisal institution shall have the right to dissolve the contract.

Article 21 An appraisal institution shall, based on business needs, establish a professional risk fund or voluntarily take out professional liability insurance to improve its risk prevention mechanism.

Article 22 A client shall have the right to independently choose an appraisal institution that meets the requirements of this Law, and no organization or individual may illegally restrict or interfere with such choice.
Where an appraisal matter involves two or more parties, all parties shall negotiate to engage an appraisal institution.
Where a statutory appraisal business is engaged, the appraisal institution shall be selected according to law.

Article 23 The client shall conclude an engagement contract with the appraisal institution, stipulating the rights and obligations of both parties.
The client shall pay fees to the appraisal institution in accordance with the contract, and shall not demand, accept, or demand or accept in disguised form, any kickback.
The client shall be responsible for the authenticity, completeness and legality of the ownership certificates, financial accounting information and other materials provided by it.

Article 24 For an accepted appraisal business, the appraisal institution shall assign at least two appraisal professionals to undertake it.
The client shall have the right to request the withdrawal of any appraisal professional who has a conflict of interest with the relevant parties or the appraisal subject.

Article 25 An appraisal professional shall, based on the specific circumstances of the appraisal business, conduct an on-site investigation of the appraisal subject, collect ownership certificates, financial accounting information and other materials, and verify, validate, analyze and organize them as the basis for appraisal.

Article 26 An appraisal professional shall appropriately select appraisal methods. Except where only one appraisal method may be selected in accordance with the professional practice standards, at least two appraisal methods shall be selected, and after comprehensive analysis, an appraisal conclusion shall be formed and an appraisal report prepared.
The appraisal institution shall conduct an internal review of the appraisal report.

Article 27 An appraisal report shall be signed by at least two appraisal professionals who undertook the appraisal business and affixed with the seal of the appraisal institution.
The appraisal institution and its appraisal professionals shall bear liability according to law for the appraisal reports they issue.
The client shall not collude with or instigate the appraisal institution or appraisal professionals to issue a false appraisal report.

Article 28 Where an appraisal institution conducts statutory appraisal business, it shall assign at least two appraisers of the corresponding professional category to undertake it, and the appraisal report shall be signed by at least two appraisers who undertook the business and affixed with the seal of the appraisal institution.
Article 29 The retention period for appraisal archives shall be no less than fifteen years; for statutory appraisal business, the retention period shall be no less than thirty years.
Article 30 Where a client has objections to an appraisal report, it may request the appraisal institution to provide an explanation.

Article 31 Where a client believes that an appraisal institution or appraisal professional has conducted business illegally, it may lodge a complaint or report to the relevant appraisal administrative department or trade association, and the relevant appraisal administrative department or trade association shall promptly investigate and handle the matter and respond to the client.

Article 32 The client or the user of the appraisal report shall use the appraisal report in accordance with the provisions of law and the scope of use specified in the appraisal report.
Where the client or the user of the appraisal report uses the appraisal report in violation of the preceding paragraph, the appraisal institution and the appraisal professionals shall not bear liability.

Article 33 Appraisal trade associations are self-discipline organizations of appraisal institutions and appraisal professionals, and shall exercise self-discipline management in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and their articles of association.
National appraisal trade associations shall be established by professional field in the appraisal industry, and local appraisal trade associations may be established as needed.

Article 34 The articles of association of an appraisal trade association shall be formulated by the members' congress, submitted to the registration authority for approval, and filed with the relevant appraisal administrative department.

Article 35 Appraisal institutions and appraisal professionals that join the relevant appraisal trade association shall equally enjoy the rights stipulated in the articles of association and perform the obligations stipulated therein. The relevant appraisal trade association shall publish the list of appraisal institutions and appraisal professionals that have joined the association.

Article 37 The relevant appraisal trade associations shall establish mechanisms for communication, cooperation and information sharing, formulate common codes of conduct as needed, and promote the healthy and orderly development of the appraisal industry.

Article 38 The standards for collecting membership dues by an appraisal trade association shall be adopted by the members' congress and disclosed to the public. The amount of membership dues paid by a member shall not be used as a condition for that member to hold a position in the trade association.
The collection and use of membership dues shall be subject to the supervision of the members' congress and relevant departments, and no organization or individual may embezzle, privately distribute or misappropriate such dues.

Article 39 The relevant appraisal administrative departments under the State Council shall organize the formulation of basic appraisal standards and measures for the supervision and administration of the appraisal industry.

Article 40 The relevant appraisal administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the city with districts level shall, in accordance with their respective duties, be responsible for supervising and administering the appraisal industry, imposing administrative penalties according to law on illegal acts of appraisal institutions and appraisal professionals, promptly notifying the relevant appraisal trade associations of the penalties, and disclosing such information to the public according to law.

Article 41 The appraisal administrative departments shall exercise supervision and inspection over the relevant appraisal trade associations, and shall promptly investigate and handle any problems discovered during inspection as well as complaints and reports against the associations.
Article 42 No appraisal administrative department may, in violation of the provisions of this Law, restrict an appraisal institution from conducting business according to law.

Article 43 No appraisal administrative department shall have any personnel or financial connection with an appraisal trade association or appraisal institution, nor shall it use its authority to solicit business for an appraisal institution.

Article 45 Where an appraisal professional, in violation of the provisions of this Law, signs a false appraisal report, the relevant appraisal administrative department shall order a suspension from practice for not less than two years but not more than five years; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; if the circumstances are serious, a suspension from practice for not less than five years but not more than ten years shall be ordered; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law, and the person shall be prohibited from engaging in appraisal business for life.

Article 46 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, any person engages in appraisal business in the name of an appraisal institution without industrial and commercial registration, the administrative department for industry and commerce shall order cessation of the illegal activity; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains shall also be imposed.

Article 48 Where an appraisal institution, in violation of the provisions of this Law, issues a false appraisal report, the relevant appraisal administrative department shall order suspension of business for not less than six months but not more than one year; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the administrative department for industry and commerce shall revoke the business license; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 49 Where an appraisal institution or appraisal professional, within one year, has been subjected to penalties other than suspension of business or suspension from practice three times in total for violating the provisions of this Law, the relevant appraisal administrative department may order suspension of business or suspension from practice for not less than one year but not more than five years.

Article 50 Where an appraisal professional, in violation of the provisions of this Law, causes losses to the client or other relevant parties, the appraisal institution with which he or she works shall bear compensation liability according to law. After fulfilling the compensation liability, the appraisal institution may seek recourse against the appraisal professional who acted with intent or gross negligence.

Article 51 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person who should have engaged an appraisal institution to conduct a statutory appraisal fails to do so, the relevant department shall order rectification; if the person refuses to rectify, a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 500,000 shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be given sanctions according to law; if losses are caused, compensation liability shall be borne according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 53 Where an appraisal trade association violates the provisions of this Law, the relevant appraisal administrative department shall give a warning and order rectification; if the association refuses to rectify, the matter may be reported to the registration authority, which shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 54 Where any staff member of a relevant administrative department or an appraisal trade association, in violation of the provisions of this Law, abuses his or her power, neglects his or her duty, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, he or she shall be given sanctions according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 55 This Law shall come into force as of December 1, 2016.
